answer: The umber multiplier is published, charged in grove, and nebula lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 17 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 560 identities would post 4129 proofs and burn roughly 56 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
